newsitem.title: USA: Wet, muddy fields hamper Kansas fieldwork.
newsitem.headline: Wet, muddy fields hamper Kansas fieldwork.

text.p: Kansas farmers made only limited progress with fall harvest and wheat seedings as wet, muddy fields prevailed during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.

Because weeks of delays have pushed back planting, little additional wheat acreage is expected to be seeded this fall, the report said. Until now, farmers had intended to seed additional acres in central and southeastern Kansas.
Wheat was emerged on 99 percent of Kansas acreage, versus 98 percent last week, 97 percent last year and 96 percent on average.
Kansas wheat was rated 90 percent good to excellent, versus 90 percent at that level last week.
Corn was 99 percent harvested versus 99 last week, 100 last year and the average of 98 percent.
Sorghum was 97 percent harvested, versus 95 last week, 100 last year and the average of 93 percent. Soybeans were 94 percent harvested, versus 92 last week, 100 last year and 99 on average.
Pasture condition was rated 74 percent good to excellent, versus 69 at that level last week.
